questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Ride on the shoulder away from traffic.

questions.explanation: To ride safely on a slippery surface, slow down and use both brakes when needed. Avoid sudden movements. Be careful on oily areas, shaded spots, dirt, gravel, and bridges—these have less traction.

questions.question: Space around your motorcycle helps you to:
questions.explanation: Space around your motorcycle gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. You need this space to maneuver safely.

questions.question: Most crashes happen in daylight. To be more visible, you should:

options.text: Weave back and forth on the road.

questions.explanation: Most crashes happen during the day. Always wear bright clothing when riding to stay visible, even during daylight hours.

questions.question: Only ____ can remove alcohol from your body.
questions.explanation: Only time reduces alcohol in your body. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot reduce alcohol levels or make you sober. They may keep you awake, but they do not change your blood alcohol level.

questions.question: Since most crashes happen during daylight, you should:

options.text: Ride on the shoulder and avoid traffic.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight. Always wear bright clothing when riding so other drivers see you, even during the day.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have:

options.text: Brakes in the front and rear.
Three brakes: front, rear, and emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brakes in the front and rear.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes—one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: When riding in a group:

options.text: You need at least nine riders.
Split into two or more groups if you have more than four or five riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Split into two or more groups if you have more than four or five riders.
questions.explanation: Small groups are safer than large groups. Small groups are easier for other drivers to pass, less likely to separate, and riders don't need to rush to catch up. Split into smaller groups if you have more than four or five riders.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Skip your jacket if it's warm.
Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding, even in warm weather. It protects you and helps prevent dehydration. Always wear long pants and tuck in your shoelaces so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: To prevent injury when riding on a slippery surface, you should:
questions.explanation: Slow down on slippery surfaces. Sudden movements can cause your motorcycle to skid. Do not ride on the shoulder to escape a slippery road.

questions.question: If you wait one hour after one drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Alcohol won't affect your riding skills.
Alcohol effects may still be present.
You will be fine if you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still be present.
questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can still build up in your system even with one drink per hour. This can still affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: What is the most important thing you can do to survive a crash?

options.text: Lay the motorcycle down before hitting an obstacle.
Wear a helmet that is fastened securely.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a helmet that is fastened securely.
questions.explanation: Wearing an approved helmet, face protection, and protective clothing greatly increases your chances of surviving a crash. A helmet makes you three times more likely to survive head injuries, even at low speeds.

questions.question: What is the best lane position?

options.text: The one that lets you travel the fastest.
The one that allows you to draft off other vehicles.
The one that allows other drivers to see you.
The one that places you in other vehicles' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: The one that allows other drivers to see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps other drivers see you. It should also help you see others, avoid wind blasts and blind spots, and give you space to escape if a hazard appears. Your position should keep other drivers from sharing your lane and maximize your safety space.

questions.question: Can common drugs like cold tablets affect your ability to ride safely?

options.text: Yes, they can affect your ability to safely ride a motorcycle.
No, they usually won't affect your ability to safely ride.
No, they pose no risk to your riding ability.
No, they are always safe because they are sold over-the-counter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they can affect your ability to safely ride a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Almost all drugs, including over-the-counter medicines, can affect your ability to ride safely. Always learn about the side effects of any drug before you ride.

questions.question: Which is not important when choosing a motorcycle helmet?

options.text: The helmet meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
The helmet fits snugly all around your head.
The helmet has no cracks or loose padding.

questions.explanation: Check that your helmet meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snugly around your head, and has no damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. How it looks is not important for safety.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to handle differently while you ride, what should you do?

options.text: Pull over and check your tires.
Pull over and check the chain.
Pull over and check the windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check your tires.
questions.explanation: A change in how your motorcycle handles may mean a tire has failed. If you feel any change in handling, pull over safely and check your tires right away.

questions.question: Are intersections usually safe or dangerous for riders?

options.text: Safe because there is lots of traffic.

questions.explanation: Intersections are dangerous because they have the most conflicts between motorcyclists and other drivers.

questions.question: What will goggles protect?

options.text: Your face as well as a face shield would.
Your face as well as a windshield would.

questions.explanation: Goggles protect only your eyes, not your face. A face shield is better because it protects your whole face. A windshield does not provide enough protection.

questions.question: The body eliminates about one drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks likely remain in their body?
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals about four drinks remaining in the body.

questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear has an effect similar to what?
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows your motorcycle, similar to applying the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: When should you wear a jacket while riding a motorcycle?

options.text: No matter what the weather is.
Only if you will ride longer than half an hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter what the weather is.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding, even in warm weather. It protects you from the sun and helps prevent dehydration in hot weather.
